chain.g: to separate out, sift, choose, select, evaluate, try a legal case
to choose, pick out or separate from others, sift, cull

ety.text: From Middle English trien (“to separate out, sift, choose, select, evaluate, try a legal case”), from Anglo-Norman trier, triher, triere (“to divide, separate, choose, select, prove, determine, try a case”), Old French trier (“to choose, pick out or separate from others, sift, cull”), of uncertain origin. Cognate with Occitan triar (“to choose, sort, scrutinise, peel”), Catalan triar (“to pick, choose, decide”).
From Middle English trye, trie, probably from Old French trié, past participle of Old French trier (“to try”).

senses.d: To attempt; to endeavour. Followed by infinitive.
ex: I tried to rollerblade, but I couldn’t.
Can you start the car? —I'll try (to).

senses.d: To separate (precious metal etc.) from the ore by melting; to purify, refine.
ex: […]euery feend his buſie paines applyde, / To melt the golden metall, ready to be tryde.

senses.d: To winnow; to sift; to pick out; frequently followed by out.
ex: to try out the wild corn from the good
the wylde corne, beinge in shap and greatnesse lyke to the good, if they be mengled, with great difficultie will be tried out

senses.d: To extract oil from blubber or fat; to melt down blubber to obtain oil
To extract wax from a honeycomb
To make an experiment. Usually followed by a present participle.
ex: I tried mixing more white paint to get a lighter shade.

senses.d: To put to test.
ex: I shall try my skills on this.
“So mousie shall only find tins on the floor now,” thought Miss Mapp. “Mousie shall try his teeth on tins.”

senses.d: To test someone's patience.
ex: You are trying my patience.
Don't try me.

senses.d: To fight or to make an attempt at an attack.
ex: You wouldn't dare and try me!
You fixin' to try something, fool?

senses.d: To receive an imminent attack; to take.
ex:
Mona: Try this vampire bolt on for size!
Cedric: Why don't you try this alien bolt?

senses.d: An attempt.
ex: I gave unicycling a try but I couldn’t do it.
When Papillon makes his last impossible try for freedom they embrace with the tendresse of lovers, however manly and platonic.

senses.d: An act of tasting or sampling.
ex: I gave sushi a try but I didn’t like it.

senses.d: A score in rugby league and rugby union, analogous to a touchdown in American football.
ex: Today I scored my first try.

senses.d: A screen, or sieve, for grain.
ex: They will not passe thorough the holes of the sieve, ruddle or trie, if they be narrow.

senses.d: A field goal or extra point
A move that almost solves a chess problem, except that Black has a unique defense.
A block of code that may trigger exceptions the programmer expects to catch, usually demarcated by the keyword try.
Fine, excellent.
ex: But he her ſuppliant hands, thoſe hands of gold, / And eke her feete, thoſe feete of ſiluer trye, […] Chopt off […].
